label: L=3 sequences, last two copy outputs (recall 1 and 2)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost entirely in length-3 sequences at the second and third copy steps (t=4,5; recall_idx 1-2). Recall_idx 2 (final output, two steps after <DEL>) is strongest and holds ~71% of the mass; recall_idx 1 holds ~20%. A weak tail fires on L=4 at recall_idx 2 (t=6, mostly low activation) and a few L=9 final steps. Never fires in the original phase, on the delimiter step, or on recall_idx 0. Within the L=3 window, firing depends on token identity: stronger when the fed-back input is a letter such as o/a/d/u, and weaker or absent when the sequence has digits or repeated tokens. Adding digit or repeat conditions did not improve F1. So the predicate catches ~91% of activation mass but only about half of the predicted steps actually fire.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=6: o, a, d, p; t=12: o, a, k, v; t=11: o, a, y) and the previous input (most: w, c, j, u, a, b; least: m, y, x, h); timing cues that raise it most: L=3, L=3 & t=5, L=3 & t=4.
